title: The Layoffs Aren't Slowing Down. Neither Should Your Headcount Plan.
summary: Here's a stat that should stop you mid-scroll: tech companies have cut more than 210,000 jobs so far in 2026 — already past all of 2025, with months still to go. Oracle alone has eliminated close to 30,000 roles. Amazon, Meta, Microsoft followed. And almost every one of them said the same thing: this isn't about a bad quarter. It's AI.
body_markdown:
## **The Old Signal Doesn't Work Anymore**


Layoffs used to track revenue trouble. You could look at a cut and know what it meant. That correlation is gone. Microsoft's own chief people officer said the roles they eliminated weren't being replaced by AI — they were eliminated because AI changed the work around them. Coinbase, Salesforce, Block have said versions of the same thing. These aren't distress signals. They're reallocations.


Which means the plan you build in January and lock until next year's budget cycle is already the wrong tool.


## **Growth and Headcount Are Coming Apart**


Oracle's cuts hit cloud and sales hardest — its fastest-growing lines of business, not its weakest. If your headcount model still assumes revenue growth means proportional headcount growth, this year is telling you that assumption is broken. Some functions absorb AI-assisted workflows. Some don't. Plan by function, not by top line.


## **Three Things Worth Changing Right Now**


**Stop planning once a year.** HR and Finance need to see the same real-time headcount and budget picture, so a "what if we pause this req" conversation takes an afternoon, not a planning offsite.


**Separate restructuring cost from steady-state budget.** Oracle has already booked over $2 billion in restructuring expense this year. Mixing that into your ongoing headcount forecast just makes the next forecast wrong too.


**Take care of the people who stay.** Every round creates survivor anxiety, and in a year where AI displacement is a daily headline, that anxiety compounds fast. Clear pay bands and predictable review cycles are one of the few things HR fully controls right now — use them.


## **The Real Fix Is Alignment, Not Software**


The teams handling this well aren't the ones with the fanciest dashboard. They're the ones where HR and Finance are already looking at the same numbers, so nobody's reconciling spreadsheets after the decision's already been made.


If your headcount data still lives in three tabs and a slide from last quarter, you're not behind on tooling. You're behind on the conversation.
